To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the simultaneous RNA interference of MMP9 and cathep-sinB has a synergistic effect in inhibiting the growth, invasion and angiogenesis of glioblastoma cells.
RNAi mediated inhibition of MMP 9 or cathepsinB gene expression in glioma cells significantly reduces glioma cell invasion, angiogenesis and tumor growth in vivo.

the RNAi mediated targeting and inhibition of MMP 9, cathepsin-B and their proteolytic cascaded in human glioblastoma cells and in vivo glioma models significantly reduced glioma tumor growth, angiogenesis, invasion, migration, and metastasis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new approach to treat glioma by targeting MMP 9 and/or cathepsinB gene expression using RNA interference.
developing a novel approach to target the expression of multiple genes in glioblastomas.
the development of a new therapeutic modality for glioma treatment based on RNAi technology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
RNAi mediated targeting and silencing of MMP 9 or cathepsinB alone or in combination has potential application for treating human gliomas.

RNAi mediated simultaneous inhibition of MMP 9, and cathepsins B gene expression in gliomas can reduce tumor growth, angiogenesis, and cell invasion, and may be a useful approach for the treatment of gliomas.
the RNAi based approach for the simultaneous inhibition of MMP 9 as well as cathepsin gene expression in glioma cells has the potential to be developed as a novel treatment for human brain tumors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
RNAi mediated targeting MMP 9 and Cathepsin B in glioblastomas would be a potential therapeutic strategy for the treatment of glioblastomas.

we have demonstrated for the first time, the use of RNAi to target two different proteases in the same cell to reduce glioblastoma invasion, tumor growth, angiogenesis and tumor cell migration in vitro and in a xenograft model of glioblastoma.
the combined RNAi of MMP 9 & cathepsinB has the ability to block the tumor growth & invasion of glioma cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the simultaneous targeting of two genes involved in the same pathway can be a better strategy for the treatment of cancer.
simultaneous targeting of multiple genes involved in tumor growth, angiogenesis and invasion using hpRNA triggered RNA interference is an effective therapeutic approach to treat gliomas.

RNAi mediated inhibition of MMP 9 cathepsin b gene expression in glioma cells can be achieved using a single plasmid construct, and that the inhibition of these two genes in glioma cells reduces the invasive behavior of glioma cells, reduces tumor cell cell interaction, reduces tumor growth and invasion and reduces angiogenesis in vivo.
